summary: The quest-nemesis death branch is skipped in JavaScript. C calls quest.c:nemdead before dropping the dead monster’s inventory; that function invokes the quest pager, whose nhl_init executes nhlib.lua’s three-item alignment shuffle. JavaScript records the nemdead call as unported and reaches an unrelated rn2(6) drop-path draw instead.

source.branch: When a monster with MS_NEMESIS dies and killed_nemesis is still false, set killed_nemesis before calling qt_pager("killed_nemesis"); later calls return without pager output or random draws.
callers: mon.c:m_detach (called from mondead on due_to_death before stinky_nemesis and relobj)
dependencies: questpgr.c:qt_pager (existing JS port initializes nhlib.lua through comPagerCore)

evidence: nethack-c/upstream/src/quest.c:107-114 — nemdead() guards on killed_nemesis, sets the flag, then calls qt_pager("killed_nemesis").
nethack-c/upstream/src/mon.c:2768-2776 — m_detach() calls nemdead() for a dying MS_NEMESIS before stinky_nemesis() and relobj().
nethack-c/upstream/src/questpgr.c:630-633 and nhlua.c:2295-2357 — qt_pager() reaches com_pager_core(), which creates a Lua state and loads nhlib.lua.
nethack-c/upstream/dat/nhlib.lua:17-25 — the top-level shuffle consumes rn2(3) then rn2(2) while permuting align.

js/mon.js:m_detach — the nemesis branch maps to note_unported("quest.c nemdead") and then continues to relobj(); js/quest.js has no nemdead implementation, while js/questpgr.js already implements pager initialization.
